Answers for the queries by hand handout. Each answer is followed by one SQL
query that produces it. Other queries can give the same result.

## The tables

**customers**

| customer_id | first_name | last_name |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | John | Doe |
| 2 | Jane | Smith |
| 3 | Robert | Johnson |
| 4 | Sarah | Williams |

**products**

| product_id | name | price |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Silk Blouse | 89.99 |
| 2 | Denim Jeans | 79.99 |
| 3 | Cashmere Sweater | 149.99 |
| 4 | Cotton T-Shirt | 29.99 |
| 5 | Wool Coat | 199.99 |

**orders**

| order_id | customer_id | product_id | order_date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 3 | 2025-03-10 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 2025-03-12 |
| 3 | 3 | 4 | 2025-03-15 |
| 4 | 2 | 4 | 2025-03-18 |
| 5 | 1 | 2 | 2025-03-20 |
| 6 | 2 | 3 | 2025-03-25 |

{{< pagebreak >}}

**1.** Show the `first_name` and `last_name` of every customer who placed an order between 2025-03-15 and 2025-03-21. List each customer only once.

| first_name | last_name |
|---|---|
| John | Doe |
| Robert | Johnson |
| Jane | Smith |

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.first_name, c.last_name
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2025-03-15' AND '2025-03-21';
```

**2.** For every order of a product that costs more than \$80, show the customer's `first_name`, the product's `name`, and the `order_date`.

| first_name | name | order_date |
|---|---|---|
| John | Cashmere Sweater | 2025-03-10 |
| Jane | Silk Blouse | 2025-03-12 |
| Jane | Cashmere Sweater | 2025-03-25 |

```sql
SELECT c.first_name, p.name, o.order_date
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN products p  ON p.product_id  = o.product_id
WHERE p.price > 80;
```

**3.** For each product that was ordered at least once, show its `name` and `total_revenue`, its price times the number of times it was ordered, sorted from highest `total_revenue` to lowest.

| name | total_revenue |
|---|---|
| Cashmere Sweater | 299.98 |
| Silk Blouse | 89.99 |
| Denim Jeans | 79.99 |
| Cotton T-Shirt | 59.98 |

```sql
SELECT p.name, SUM(p.price) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = o.product_id
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
```

**4.** Show the `first_name` and `num_orders` of every customer who placed more than one order.

| first_name | num_orders |
|---|---|
| Jane | 3 |
| John | 2 |

```sql
SELECT c.first_name, COUNT(*) AS num_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.first_name
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```

**5.** Show the `first_name` and `last_name` of every customer who has never ordered the Cotton T-Shirt.

| first_name | last_name |
|---|---|
| John | Doe |
| Sarah | Williams |

Sarah counts: she has no orders at all, so she never ordered the T-Shirt.

```sql
SELECT first_name, last_name
FROM customers
WHERE customer_id NOT IN (
  SELECT o.customer_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN products p ON p.product_id = o.product_id
  WHERE p.name = 'Cotton T-Shirt'
);
```
